label: Run monitor
info: Report status, monthly history and validated backfill commands. Generate both HTTP In access keys after import.

name: [1] HTTP MONITOR
info: STAGE 1 - One access-key-protected route serves page, status and history at /reports-monitor using the view query parameter. Generate its access key in the VFC after import. The page reuses it for all GET requests.

name: 1.1 Route monitor request
[2] PAGE
info: STAGE 2 - Returns the self-contained page. It polls status every 10 seconds and loads one month of CSV history only when requested.

name: [3] STATUS
info: STAGE 3 - Returns compact snapshots only: report-day checkpoints, PBI build and listener state, Config state, plus a derived STUCK state after 30 minutes without a checkpoint.

name: 3.1 Build status JSON
[4] HISTORY REQUEST
info: STAGE 4 - Validates the flow and month, lists one log folder, and reads the requested monthly CSV only when it exists.

name: 4.1 Check history request
4.2 Find history file
4.3 Build history JSON
[5] ERROR RESPONSE
info: STAGE 5 - Invalid requests keep their explicit 400, 404 or 503 status and JSON error. A list-object response that is not a list returns 502.

name: [6] HISTORY NOT FOUND
info: STAGE 6 - A month with no CSV log returns 404 without starting a read-object request that could otherwise wait indefinitely.

name: [7] BACKFILL COMMAND
info: POST /reports-monitor/command validates one backfill, records an audit line, and returns 202 before the target starts. Generate this HTTP In access key separately. Connect each named BACKFILL link out to the matching link in of its report tab after import (the flows come from scripts/monitor-flows.js). A force command can run concurrently with the same flow.

name: 7.1 Validate backfill
[8] NODE ERROR
info: STAGE 8 - A data-lake node error returns a generic 502. Credentials and request keys are never copied into the response.

name: 8.1 Build error response
[9] ERRORS
info: STAGE 9 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 9.1 Describe error
[10] LOG
info: STAGE 10 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 10.1 Format log line
10.2 Build log write
[11] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 11 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.

name: 11.1 Append log rows
